chunks: Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, Hisham ibn Salim, Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar, and others narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

If people were to abandon the hajj, it would be incumbent upon the leader to compel them to perform it and to remain there. And if they were to abandon the visitation of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, it would be incumbent upon the leader to compel them to do that and to remain there. If they did not have wealth, he should spend on them from the public treasury of the Muslims.

key_terms.الْحَجَّ: the hajj pilgrimage, treated here as a rite whose abandonment cannot be tolerated publicly
key_terms.الْمُقَامِ: remaining or staying there after going
key_terms.الْوَالِي: the governing authority responsible for enforcing communal religious duties
key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury of the Muslims from which support may be given
key_terms.زِيَارَةَ: visitation, here specifically visiting the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about a ruler compelling people to perform hajj and visit the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the public and communal importance of hajj and the visitation of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It states that the wali has authority to compel performance of these rites and, where needed, support people financially from the Muslim treasury so these obligations and symbols are not abandoned.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2861 - Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, Hisham ibn Salim, Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar, and others narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"If people were to abandon the Hajj, it would be incumbent upon the leader to compel them to perform it and to remain at the sacred site. And if they were to abandon the visitation of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), it would be incumbent upon the leader to compel them to perform it and to remain there. If they did not have sufficient wealth, he should spend on them from the public treasury of the Muslims."
